RagShortTexts: The ruling elite of Picts comprised ancient aristocratic houses and military dynasties competing for feudal land and fiscal control.
Domestic politics were profoundly steered by court intrigues and noble factions resisting excessive central centralization.
Intricate matrimonial alliances and blood feuds permeated the nobility, ensuring that disputed successions frequently sparked nationwide crises.

Variants.Content: Within the opulent halls and sprawling feudal estates of Picts, the balance of domestic power remained in perilous equilibrium. Ancient lineages commanded vast agricultural latifundia, hereditary warrior retinues, and lucrative trade monopolies, acting simultaneously as imperial cornerstones and covert rivals to the throne. Court assemblies seethed with venomous factionalism, pitting entrenched senatorial aristocrats against battle-hardened military commanders who demanded greater political dominance. Behind tapestried corridors, clandestine poisonings, forged wills, and intercepted treaties dictated political ascendancy. Lesser vassals maneuvered cautiously between dominant magnates, ready to shift allegiance whenever the central authority showed signs of exhaustion or military defeat.

At the fire of the great house, guardsmen stand with their backs to the timber wall and listen to the clan chiefs argue about the cattle raids. The old warrior at the end of the bench says nothing and keeps his hand on his knife. Men on the gate know that a clan feud can begin with a single sheep stolen from the wrong pasture.

The chief of the western glens has refused to send his tribute of hides to the feast, and his son now claims the grazing rights along the river. Invite the glen chiefs to a feast at the hilltop fort and offer each a share of the new grazing rights. Make the proposal verbally, since any written pledge will be read aloud at the clan gathering and may start a blood feud.
